name: Immich
tagline: Self-hosted photo and video backup, similar to Google Photos
description: A photo and video server with mobile apps that back up your camera roll automatically. Timeline, albums, face recognition, search by content, map and sharing all run on your own hardware.
licenseNote: Every feature is free. An optional supporter licence funds development and unlocks nothing.
backing: FUTO (US) employs the core team; optional supporter purchases

maturity.rationale: Declared stable in late 2025 after years of breakneck development, and now on a predictable release cadence. Still young enough that the project itself insists you keep an independent backup.

selfHosting.summary: A well-documented Docker Compose stack: server, machine learning, PostgreSQL and a cache. The first indexing of a large library keeps the CPU busy for hours or days; after that it idles quietly.

requirements.notes: Check the current requirements page before buying hardware. Budget storage for your library plus roughly 10–20% for thumbnails and transcoded video.

managedHosting.label: PikaPods
managedHosting.note: Third-party managed hosting, billed by resource use

strengths: Mobile apps with automatic background backup, just like Google Photos
Face recognition, search by content, map and memories, all computed on your own server
Shared albums, partner sharing and public links
External libraries index folders you already have without copying them
weaknesses: No end-to-end encryption: whoever runs the server can see the photos
You are the backup. Immich is not a backup tool, and its documentation tells you to keep separate copies
Google Takeout import relies on the community tool immich-go, which works well but is not official
